Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
613 AM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat building this week with temperatures in the upper
  90s/100s and heat indices of 104-112F. Heat Advisories likely at
  times during the upcoming work week.

- Patchy fog possible during the early to mid-morning hours for at
  least the next few days.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1056 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Hot, then even hotter. Maybe some rain late in the week. The end.

Oh wait you're still here?! That pretty much sums up the forecast
period, but I'll gladly add some more context! High temperatures 
on Sunday topped out in the low to mid 90s once again, which seems
"cool" compared to what's ahead for the work week. The 596-598 
dam mid-level high (the heatdome) is currently centered near the 
intersection of TX/OK/CO/NM...so it's continuing to gradually 
nudge eastward towards the Central and Southern Plains. Going into
Monday, the heatdome begins to slide into north TX where it'll 
remain through at least midweek. 850mb temperatures will gradually
increase each day leading to a gradual climb in high 
temperatures. Expect temperatures to top out in the upper 90s to 
low 100s throughout the work week. We haven't even talked about 
everyone's favorite word this time of the year...the humidity. 

South-southwesterly to southerly surface flow should keep dew points 
elevated (low to mid 70s) closer to the coast. Further inland, we 
should see dew points mixing out into at least the upper 60s to low 
70s in the afternoons during the work week. The air temperatures 
will be high enough though that we'll still see heat indices peaking 
near or above the Heat Advisory threshold (greater than 108 degrees) 
at times this week, especially Tuesday and beyond. Speaking of Heat 
Advisories, we decided to hold off again on issuing one for Monday.
While a few sites will reach criteria again, we aren't expecting 
it to be widespread enough to warrant issuing an advisory. Tuesday
and beyond has much better potential for Heat Advisories. 

There won't be much relief overnight with low temperatures mainly in 
the upper 70s to low 80s. The atrocious humidity overnight will 
result in occasional rounds of patchy fog in the early to mid 
morning hours for at least the next few days. PW values decrease 
going into Monday closer to the 10th percentile (~1.36") through at 
least midweek, so rain chances will be slim to none for most of the 
work week. Towards the end of the work week, the heatdome begins to 
retreat westward a bit which looks to open the door for our next 
chance of showers/storms. Yesterday we talked about how ensemble 
guidance shows the potential for surface low pressure developing in 
the Southern Plains late in the week that may bring a frontal 
boundary nearby over the weekend. The potential for this is still 
there, and the synoptic flow would support it as an an upper level 
trough pushes through the eastern CONUS over the weekend. This 
coincides with increasing moisture, and thus we do have rain chances 
in the forecast for the weekend! To get there though, we'll have to 
make it through the triple digit heat of the work week...and even 
then it's not likely that all of us will see rain!

With heat indices expected to be near or above Heat Advisory 
criteria over the next several days, please keep heat safety at the 
top of your minds for any plans that you make (especially if 
outdoors). Know the signs of heat-related illnesses, stay hydrated 
(with water), take frequent breaks from the heat, wear loose/light-
colored clothing and sunscreen, and ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS LOOK before 
you LOCK your vehicle. Don't forget about your pets as well! If the 
ground is too hot for the palm of your hand, then it is too hot for 
their paws. 

Batiste

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
619 AM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat is expected this week with temperatures in the 
  upper 90s to 100s and heat indices of 106-110F. 

- A Heat Advisory is in affect today for the eastern parts of the
  forecast area. With further advisories likely through the week.

- Later in the week, upper ridging begins to lose its control
  overhead, allowing temps to moderate slightly and rain chances 
  to return to the forecast.
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1205 AM CDT Mon Jul 27 2026

A significant upper level ridge extending from California to the 
southeastern US will continue to dominate the synoptic weather 
pattern through the next few days, resulting in a repetitive 
forecast of hot and dry conditions. Today, highs will reach into the 
mid to upper 90s while heat indices will top out in the mid to upper 
100s through the afternoon. As a result, a Heat Advisory has been 
issued for those parishes along I-49 and into lower Acadiana from 
noon through 7PM today. Elsewhere, heat indices will near the 108 
mark in a few locations however, most areas are expected to remain 
below advisory criteria. Tomorrow and Wednesday, much of the same 
sweltering heat is expected, with more Heat Advisories likely to be 
issued, possibly area-wide. With ridging aloft maintaining control, 
no rainfall is expected through Wednesday.  

Thursday into the weekend, upper ridging begins to weaken slightly 
and retreat westward, becoming centered more over the Four Corners 
region. In its place, a strong upper trough becomes carved out 
across the Eastern Seaboard through the end of the work week. As the 
ridge loses some influence over the CWA, small rain chances begin
to return to the forecast particularly across the eastern half of
the region Thurs through Sat. In addition, slightly better rain 
chances and more cloud cover will keep temps in check somewhat 
through the end of the week, mainly keeping us out of heat 
advisory territory. Moving into next weekend, the initial E CONUS 
ridge will be ejecting off into the Atlantic, while a northern 
stream shortwave looks to dive across the Great Lakes and drop 
southward, carving out another trough across the E CONUS around 
the end of the forecast period. This will bring a larger scale
weakness overhead aloft and in turn a further uptick in rain 
chances later in the weekend.
